utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. For the sake of the report, in relation to Witness VG-18, let me inform you that it was only at 7.33 p.m. last evening that we received the proofing list for that witness which contains very significant and extensive modifications which makes our preparation more difficult. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll ask Ms. Sartorio to address the particulars of it, but I would remind Mr. Cepic and the Chamber that this was the witness who I rescheduled earlier in the week because she became ill after she arrived here. I know Ms. Sartorio was working with her all day yesterday and given the length of time between her statement and now, she had made some changes. I have not seen the document. I don't know how many changes were made to the statement. I'll leave it to the Chamber to decide what's warranted, but I do make the point that this was the woman that became ill after she arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can I ask the court deputy to have somebody look at the computers. We don't have the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long would this witness take, Mr. Groome, and do you have another witness that's available?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The only two witnesses remaining for this week are VG-18 and VG-84. They are mother and son. Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The point that Mr. Cepic made relates to VG-18.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. That's the second witness for today. I -- it's possible that we may only begin her evidence today and may have to conclude it on Monday, or if the Court -- another suggestion I might make is the video that I introduced yesterday is approximately 15 to 20 minutes long. At some point we'll have to look at that video. It was introduced yesterday. That's something also at that we could do to give Mr. Cepic and Mr. Alarid some time if the Court feels that is warranted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber's ruling is that we should proceed, and we'll make any adjustments as -- as necessary, but I had wanted on behalf of the Chamber, Mr. Groome, to raise a matter relating to the witnesses for next week, because we observe that Mr. Vasiljevic is down for a portion of Wednesday and all day Thursday, which might suggest that we might not have enough time to finish him in the course of the week, and we wonder whether he shouldn't be called earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think this is a good illustration of how difficult it is to estimate witnesses. I actually thought that that might be too much time for him. So we have the flexibility. Mr. Cepic informs me that Mr. Domazet, who has been hired by the registry to represent him is asking that he not be taken until Wednesday, but if we have him on Wednesday, I'm more than willing to move back witnesses to make whatever adjustments so that we have a full opportunity to hear him. I don't believe he could go further than Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we proceed there is a matter that I must bring to your attention and I ask that we go into private session for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration -- the witness is still under the declaration that he had made.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: May I begin, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good morning, VG-84.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer kindly to call up Exhibit P74 and to turn to e-court page 4, please. Once we get to page 4, perhaps we could focus on the upper half of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, do you see the -- your statement on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you see the paragraph which begins "About one-half to one hour after Mitar left"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to read over that paragraph to yourself and then I will ask you a few follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to read it aloud?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No. You can just read it over to yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. There's no need for me to read it. You can go ahead with the questions. I have sufficient knowledge about all this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In this paragraph you mentioned Sredoje Lukic, and you described his actions. Can you tell the Chamber how did you know Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two -- or, rather, three men came to the house, the Memic house. There was several others behind the house, but I wasn't able to observe how many of them were behind the house, and there were several in front of the house. Two men came into the house, Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic. There was one elderly man and all my neighbours and friends who were in the house knew him, and 20 to 25 per cent of them knew Sredoje Lukic who was allegedly a policeman. I was a child at the time, so I didn't know him. We had heard of him -- do you want me to go on explaining?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard of him while we were in our village, the village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, I'm sorry to interrupt you. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Let's just take it step-by-step. As you see, your statement is on the screen in front of everybody, and we can all read it in English, including the Judges, so it's also in evidence, so this will be considered in detail. I'm simply going to focus you on a few small follow-up questions. So you say that you -- that 20 to 25 per cent of your neighbours who were in the Memic house with you knew Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both of them. Both Sredoje and Milan. I'm telling you how it was roughly. I don't know the details. I was just under 14. I wasn't checking who knew him, but between 20 to 25 per cent of those who were in the house knew the two men who came into the room -- or, rather, the three men, because the third one remained in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Why would you have believed your neighbours that this was in fact Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, why wouldn't they believe us? This was not a town of 1 million. Some 10.000 inhabited it. It was a small town.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, how did you know Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same was true for him. I saw him for the first time there, but I had heard of him in my village of Koritnik, and though I saw him for the first time in the house, there were others with me who knew him, perhaps got to know him the same way I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What -- on what basis do you believe that they knew Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were girls in the house who used to go to school with him, so they used to be schoolmates, and they -- they seemed like perfect strangers. It was the changing times that did their thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To your knowledge was there anyone else by the name of Milan Lukic in Visegrad during 1992, other than the one you're referring to now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the court officer please focus on the middle paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: It begins with the words "After they (Sredoje and his group) left."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, I'll ask you just to take a moment, please, to read through that paragraph before I ask you a few follow-up questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can go ahead with the questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any other members of the group other than Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than Sredoje there was Milan with him and another soldier who I didn't know. He was in the house and there were several others outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, both in the statement, and the witness confirmed here today clearly that he hadn't known Milan and Sredoje Lukic before he got to know them as he got into the house, and my learned friend has been putting her question and it was formulated differently.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in this paragraph which is in evidence, the witness describes Sredoje Lukic. He previously testified that he was informed by his neighbours who were detained with him that that was in fact Sredoje Lukic, and based on his understanding he describes Sredoje Lukic and his group, and in the middle of this paragraph he describes there were about 10 to 15 soldiers and he's mentioning soldiers. So the question was: Did you recognise any other members of the group which is referred to in this paragraph. The question stems directly from the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I believe the question is unobjectionable. It will be for you, Mr. Cepic, in cross-examination to seek to impugn the witness's knowledge of Sredoje Lukic. You can question him as to the basis for his knowledge and seek to destroy. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, this paragraph describes the trajectory from the Memic house to the Omeragic house. You mention in this paragraph that there was a light at the Omeragic house. What about along the path from the Memic house to the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Memic house is some 30 metres away from the Omeragic house. This is an approximation. As we got out of the Memic house - I'm describing it the way I saw it - and as I was on my way to the Omeragic house, there was some light outside the house. There were torches, and there was light coming from the surrounding houses. This made it possible for me to see quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Why -- why do you think that the Omeragic house was the house which was chosen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was right next to a creek, and this would muffle the voices and the wailing of the women and the children.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the court officer please go to the bottom of the page, focusing on the bottom half.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, I'd like to focus you on the bottom paragraph on that page. Would you like to read it through briefly before I ask you some follow-up questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: As you were hiding behind the tree with your mother, do you recall hearing anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard the crying of the children, of the elderly women, moans, shouts. I heard a blast and shooting. The house was engulfed in flames. I didn't see much, though, because I ducked my head. I was trying to make sure that I stay alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To your recollection, how many children under your age at the time, so under 13, were burned to death on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 10 to 15. There was even a two-day-old baby that her mother gave birth to in the nearby forests.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the court officer call up 65 ter 178.52. For the information of the Chamber, this is a photograph. The photograph was taken on the 1st of September of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, do you recognise what is shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Before I ask the witness to mark the photograph, would it be possible to admit the unmarked photograph so that we can refer to it with other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The photograph will become Exhibit number P77.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the court usher to assist the witness, please, in marking the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, can you identify the Memic house on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you kindly mark that location, the Memic house, with an M for Memic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you identify the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The witness has marked the Omeragic house with an O.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you please trace the path from the Memic house to the Omeragic house with an arrow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And can you circle the window you jumped out of with your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Please now kindly mark the approximate location on the creek where you and your mother hid behind the tree once you had escaped, and please mark that location with an X.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the creek, and to make it clear, this is how the creek runs, and this is the tree. It was a pear tree, I believe, under which -- or behind which my mother and I hid.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, could you please place your pseudonym at the bottom of the photo. You can just write "VG-84."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And could I admit this marked photo, please. I tender this marked photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will become Exhibit number P78, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer, please, to call up 65 ter 175.7. For the information of the Chamber, this is a still which is taken from the 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, do you recognise what is shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A house -- or, rather, the Omeragic house.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I tender this unmarked photo into evidence so we can use it with other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit P79, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, could you please, on this photograph, trace the path along which you and the other detainees approached the Omeragic house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And can you now please mark with a V the door through which you entered, V for "vrata," for "door."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And could you now please put an X at the location on the creek, the approximate location, where you hid with your mother behind the tree.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beyond the creek. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd ask you again to please place your pseudonym at the bottom of this photo, "VG-84" at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And with that, Your Honours, I tender this marked photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Marked photo will become Exhibit number P80.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I request private session for the last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: (redacted) And of course there were other people there, too, who had been in the house before who I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What is your most vivid memory of that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I remember all of it. I'm 30 now, and I still remember everything, the crying of the children, the wailing of the women and men, the blasts, the -- the shots from firearms and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can return to open session, and I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. 84.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: My name is Jason Alarid and I represent Mr. Milan Lukic. I'd like to ask you a few questions regarding your statements. Obviously they've been introduced into evidence, and some of the things that you've talked about in those statements and today. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you know the first thing that comes to me when you say how vivid this is in your mind, it must have been a terrible experience for a young boy to go through that I can't even begin to imagine not having been through it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you escaped this tragedy with your mother into the creek, that was at the -- that was at the very beginning of the incident, wasn't it? The fire had just started --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. The fire had already caught in the home, and there were grenades blasting, and had there been more, I would not be sitting here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Actually, yes, sir, that's what I meant, and all I say, though, is that was it at the very beginning that this grenade, and you received the shrapnel in your head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There wasn't just one grenade. There were several of them falling. There was fire from -- there was shots from firearms. And the fire, the way it started burning, it wasn't like you -- you had a small spark, and it did not develop slowly. You could escape from such a fire. But there were -- there were weapons there. There were blasts from grenades. And let me clarify this. I ended up only 50 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the -- in looking at the photographs that the Prosecutor showed you, it appears that there's a lot of vegetation on the slope into the creek, in the bottom of the creek, and obviously up the other side of the creek to the pear tree where you were able to hide yourselves. Is that -- was it the same back then or similar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There wasn't anything. There was just the undergrowth, and the only tree that was there was the one we hid behind, because this was a maintained garden. The owner of the house perhaps left the house a month earlier, but it had been tended before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, and would it be fair to say where you and your mom were hiding afterwards, it was able to protect you from both -- from the people on the other side of the ravine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would it protect me? I was only on the other side of the creek. You were able to see the house and everything. It's just that we didn't dare watch what was happening. I ducked my head. I almost buried it in the ground. There were people with torches around. There were houses around from where the light was coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm probably using the wrong words and when it translates it even gets more confused. I'm not trying to put words in your mouth, trust me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What I'm more concerned about is really that there was something about where you were able to hide that protected you from these people across the way, torches or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. This question has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll allow him to answer it. Give us the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a tree, sir. Whether it was a peach tree or a pear tree, I don't know. Had it not been for this tree, I would have been killed perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How much time do you think had elapsed between when that fire first rose up to the grenade that injured your head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, not more than five minutes. Five minutes. Maybe not even five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, see, this is why sometimes reading things on paper don't always give a good picture of things, because when I read the statement, it seemed like it happened very quickly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, I know. Okay. Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it felt like from reading it that once the insanity and chaos started you -- the only reason you survived was you were able to get out quickly. Otherwise, you would have shared the same fate as the people in the room.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same. That's true. And because I managed to -- to grab the opportunity before the person who is -- who came under the window, who started shooting at people. There were people who were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the person that came under the window and was shooting at people and wounding people, you weren't able to recognise him in the chaos, that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's what I said in all my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just trying to -- to run for my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Absolutely. And another mother and son were able to escape around the same time as you. Were they before you or after you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another mother -- except for this mother and the son, there was another mother who was the first to break the window and jump out, and later on I jumped and another child was with me. Actually, a friend of mine. I don't remember whether I was the first or was he before me. His mother was the fourth person to jump out, and she was wounded. You know that. You had an opportunity to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did. And so was your mom the first one out the window? Even though someone else broke the window, your mom was first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was another window. Maybe somebody jumped out of it. I didn't pay attention anyway. The window that I jumped out of and that I encircled on the photograph, my mother was the first to jump out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And from where you were -- so it was pretty lucky that you were able to be at the window right when this chaos started.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in the middle of the house. There was a big table in the middle of the house. I was just a child, a 14-year-old boy. I couldn't imagine what was going to happen to me. I couldn't imagine that I was going to die in a fire. I don't think I have to tell you any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I really don't want to talk too much, because I know this is extremely painful for you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If necessary, I am at your service here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, from where you were in the table in the middle of the room, how many people were between you and the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was fully packed. The room was of such size. It wasn't a big room. I don't know exactly how big it was, but people were cram-packed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when the -- is it fair to say that you reacted to move towards your mother and the window when the fire started or before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when it all started. Why not -- why would I go before that? I was feeling fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The only reason I thought you might have gone before that because it was probably very scary in the dark after they had shut all your family members in this room and maybe you would have wanted to be closer to her and I didn't know because I couldn't tell from reading.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sitting on that table. My mother was already ready close to the window. She was an adult and she knew what was in the offing. I was just a child. Only when the fire started and the grenades did I realise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And a sad fact is that -- well, there were probably people also between your mother and the door as well because it was so packed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were people between the table where I was and my mother. Actually, the window. There were many people, but when the detonations and the shooting and the fire started, everybody lay on the ground. I just can't describe this situation to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I don't want to put you through much more and we'll move out of this room as quick as we can. Tragically, the people that were between the door and your mother probably helped protect you and your mom and allowed you that brief opportunity to escape. Isn't that fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the only reason I said that was is because they were sort of a shield between the fire that started by the door, and even some of the shrapnel, probably, was blocked by other people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would the -- did the people in the room make it difficult for you to see out the door when the fire started? Were you able to see the door open and close or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. This is a misrepresentation of the witness's statement. The witness's statement is that the door closed behind him when he entered the house. The door was closed. That's in the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The only reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reformulate, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wasn't looking at the door. The door was closed, sir. Whether it was locked or not, you can find it in the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's exactly -- I mean, many people saw this from different angles, and some people may have seen the door open, and I was wondering if you saw that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So the first thing that shocked you, of course, was the fire and then the explosion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The door was blasted out and the fire started immediately. I don't know what they did, how they did that. And this was followed by explosions and by shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I want to back up a little bit in time to the procession from the one house to the other house. Can we do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicate that there were a couple people obviously that you named in your statement, three people in fact. You mentioned Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, and Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned Mitar Vasiljevic in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Mitar Vasiljevic, the first time you had ever laid eyes on him was earlier in the day at the Red Cross? Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, not at the Red Cross. The first time I saw him was at the Memic's house. Maybe somebody did see him there but I didn't. You can also find that in my statement, when he came in front of the Memic house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And he purported to give one of the members of your group a piece of paper that ensured safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- and he was unarmed at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was he non-threatening to the group? Did he appear back earlier that he was a friend of the group or maybe less than a friend but at least someone that wasn't a threat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What group?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your group. Your group.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What group?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your group of people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not a five-member group. That was 70 people. That was my entire village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'd better be clear, and you should say, "Your village," because this was the whole village. He didn't pose a threat to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's what I was more trying to get at as opposed to the number of people, and I apologise. I'm more important on what was your impression of this man that came to visit. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am at your disposal should you need some additional explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so this man who -- how did you come to know him as Mitar, because you were just a boy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He introduced himself. He said that he was -- name was Mitar Vasiljevic, that he came from the Red Cross, and he came -- he gave the paper to Mujo Halilovic. He purported to be a good man trying to provide safety to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, did you hear anything or know about him as a waiter in town at the Panos -- for the Panos company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a waiter at the Panos.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And had you and your family ever been served by him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was a young boy. Many people knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And after he introduced himself did people in your family and village talk about him as being a waiter, or did you come to that knowledge after the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from the people who were there, that he was a waiter. A lot of people had known him there. Being a waiter in a small town is a big deal. There were not many hotels in Visegrad, only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you recall what he was wearing, Mitar Vasiljevic, when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can find that in my statement. Whether he wore a dark suit or a camouflage uniform, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the person that you named as Milan Lukic, can you recall what he was wearing that -- that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember. I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Please tell the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was he wearing anything on his head, a hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure whether it's a yes or a no, so I'd rather say I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's a fair answer after the time that's passed. Do you recall what weapons he may have had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the person that you named as Sredoje Lukic, what do you believe he was wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some sort of camouflage uniform. Basically, they were in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember any insignias on any of these uniforms, anything to mark them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember if the person that you believe to be Sredoje, what he -- if he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How do you believe he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had some kind of automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember a hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicated on -- on direct examination that 20 to 25 per cent of the people knew Sredoje and Milan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you -- were you able to -- to make sense or make the difference between how they knew the different Lukics that you believe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me make it clear for you. Ninety-five people from my village knew about Milan, if that's helpful. They heard of him before we came to this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we were afraid to sleep in our own homes. For a month or two we slept in the forest, because we were afraid of that group. So some people had heard of them without seeing them, and some people knew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did -- kind of going back to the fear your village had been in for quite some time, isn't it true that back at the beginning --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We had lived for two months under their occupation. Since April when Visegrad fell to the Uzice Corps until the day in June when we were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was there a time when your village was attacked before -- by your neighbours before the exodus from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They attacked the whole of Visegrad, not just my village. They just passed through the village looking for weapons and we were left living in the forests or in barns, sometimes in houses, but we were living in fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know who organised the exodus from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. From the village -- from the direction of Prelovo where their headquarters was there. The gentlemen sitting behind you will know better than I do. So all the initiatives came from that. All the negotiations were launched from that headquarters involving not only my village but all the other villages as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Had you known or heard of a Dragomir Gavrilovic at that time, a neighbour of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What did you know of this Gavrilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hardly anything. He threatened my mother, but my mother will be able to tell you more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you -- you indicated that in April of 1992 the Serbian police came to your village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know the identity of these police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. The Serbian police and army were all mixed together. You couldn't distinguish them. People would come to villages for negotiations in order to evacuate the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this was before the Uzice Corps came to town or to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. That was a couple of days before we were burned in the house, and also you can find in my statements that before the Uzice Corps we had to flee.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well -- and the reason I'm confused is because I'm reading three statements. I'm reading the testimony that you gave at trial, I'm reading a statement that you were able to review with the Prosecutor that was given in 2001, but I'm also reading a statement you gave when you were 16 years old to the security forces in Sarajevo in 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you able to review the oldest statement as well as your other statements before you testified today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had an opportunity to review everything, and if anything needs clarification I am here, because I prefer to clarify things in this way. There could be some minute details, but by the way you sound, it seems that a lot is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court usher please pull up what's been uploaded as 1D10-0344, which is the English version of the 14 November 1995 statement, and 1D10-0347, which is the B/C/S version. And the first page of both, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you see the first sentence right below "Statement"? It says: "... April 1992, the Serbian police came one morning to the village ..."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sir. That's how you should ask me. That's the first time that when we left our village, when the Uzice Corps came. So that was the first time, in April, that we had to flee. And then later we came back. First we went to the village of Vrstanica, and then to the stadium in Visegrad. When the corps occupied the town, we spent the night in the Drina Hotel and then the following day we went back to our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And that's kind of what -- do you understand why I'm confused about some of the dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I really don't want to molest you in any way or bother you. I just want to get through this and you can go home.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, do you know those Serbian policemen, I guess is the question I want to ask, that first time you were forced to leave your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in April of 1992, isn't it true that you hadn't heard of Milan Lukic before the chaos began in April and the Uzice Corps were required to come into Visegrad or came into Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you went to the football stadium, in your first statement, and it's down a little bit further, you cited that there was a General Milovanovic. Is it fair that that could be corrected to Jovanovic, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I don't remember exactly, so it's either Jovanovic or Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this general, he came in a big spectacle in a helicopter. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And there were soldiers all around the stadium and your people were herded into this stadium to hear the address of this general. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People had been brought to the stadium, and they wanted to see what to do with all this crowd, because the entire right-hand bank of the Drina was there. Actually, people had come from the forest to the stadium to hear what the corps will have to say to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid. Mr. Alarid, just to let you know, you have another 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Fifteen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will wrap this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that this general indicated that he had the White Eagles in control and that you believe there was White Eagles in this stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was your understanding of the White Eagles at that time even though you were a boy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had special belts. These were special troops guarding him. They had white belts and -- and special weapons. That was only part of the Uzice Corps called the White Eagles. They were part of the Uzice Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go on this same and --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at this time, Your Honour, just so I don't forget, I'd like to tender 1D10-0344 into evidence, please, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The witness talked about some possibilities that there were some clarifications. In fact, Mr. Alarid himself referred to some issues which he believes require clarification. There was no foundation laid for the authenticity of this document, so I would -- I would hope that that could be done before it was tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, obviously we received this from the OTP, so I mean I'm assuming they know about it. We can go to signature pages if that's what we need to do, but I also believe the Prosecutor can address these matters on redirect.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just because a document comes from the OTP doesn't mean it's been authenticated by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, then I'd like additional cross-examination time, because that really slows me down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He has a lot of confidence in you, Ms. Marcus. Can you lay a foundation then for its admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mr. VG-84, you do remember giving this statement in 1995? Your mother --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your mother was present at this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you go down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. We admit it. We admit the statement. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement will become Exhibit number 1D32, Your Honours, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to page 2 of the English version, but it may be on the first page of the Serbian version. Just a moment, please. But do you recall in the statement, and maybe we don't have to go to the exact location, do you recall mentioning that Dragomir Gavrilovic was one of the same group, and you indicated that they were policemen that came to the house that night of the tragedy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember him being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you see his name on the first page of your statement? Actually, it's on page 2 of the statement, middle of the page, please. And I'm looking to the middle of that large paragraph and I see "Dragomir Gavrilovic," and I see him referred in a sentence after you referred to four policemen coming to the home.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe he was mentioned, because during the day while we were on the way he passed by us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who is Radomir Djuric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the village of Loznica. Whether he was in the police or the military, I can't tell. He came once or twice to our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, this is going to sound like a silly question, but do you remember --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember at any time during this night that the man that you believe to be Mitar Vasiljevic being on a white horse with a cast on his leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At night or during the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At any time on a white horse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only during the day, that he came outside the house, as I already described, that he gave us a piece of paper, but there was no horse there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's all I wanted to know to be honest. Do you remember the day -- the day that you started walking -- or actually, the day you were told you were going to have to evacuate your village, that was the day before that you actually walked; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. We were told on the 13th, and we -- or it was on the 12th or the 13th that we were told to leave, and then on the 14th we left, and on the evening of the 14th we were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember what day of the week the 14th was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason I ask you this is one of your clarifications that you gave that came through the Prosecutor that involved changing the date from the 13th to the 14th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may be the case. However, as far as I remember, in my last statement from 2001 when I was here it was the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, what happened between then and now that made you remember the change of one day, a calendar date?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What the witness has just said is that when he was here in 2001 he had already changed it to the 14th in his testimony. So he's referring to his prior testimony where he correctly referred to the 14th. That's why the testimony got entered into evidence without any clarification. So it's not between then and now that the time -- that the date was corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, then maybe I'll ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What happened between giving your statement on here on the 20th of January, 2001, and your testimony on -- in October of 2001? What happened that would jog your memory to change a calendar day that you had memorialised some time before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps where the statement says the 13th it may have been the result of a mistranslation. I don't know what could have happened. I will remember that date, the 14th of June, for the rest of my life, just as I remember my birth date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do have a lot of questions, and maybe I will request additional time for this witness. I'll try to do my best in a short period of time, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I have to address you by that number, not because I wish to but because that's the rules.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let me first introduce myself. My name is Djuro Cepic, and I represent this gentleman, Sredoje Lukic, seated behind me. I'll kindly ask you to help me clarify certain matters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm here for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Before I start putting any questions to you, let me tell you that I truly understand the pain and the suffering you and your mother experienced, and please accept the condolences both on my part and on the part of the members of my team for the loss of your family members.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please listen to my questions carefully. Think them over before you give me an answer, and please give me clear and concise, brief answers so that we can complete this as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you that my client, Mr. Sredoje Lukic, was not in Visegrad on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I put to you that he was not in Visegrad and that he did not take part in that incident. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't understand. Nobody can. Nobody who was not there can understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I put it to you that this was the case of a mistaken identity, and we will get to that later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your business. You should try and see that through.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you follow the start of this trial in the media, over the radio, the TV, or the press?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I've had quite enough of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I have to ask you this: Why did you refuse me the interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the need for it? You have the statements. Everything is clear. If something is not clear to you, I'm here. I can explain it to you all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In 1992 you were 13, just under 14, therefore, and you attended the Prelovo primary school; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the course of your earlier testimony and from what I was able to read in your statements, you believed that those were Milan and Sredoje Lukic according to the stories of others because you hadn't known them earlier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I said that I didn't know them before and that I had heard this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that in view of your age at the time most of the information you received came from your mother, VG-18?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Did you spend the entire time with your mother throughout the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were VG-18 -- or, rather, VG-13 and VG-38 with you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you. I don't have the necessary information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus? Did you have a point, Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I just wanted to say that the witness doesn't have the pseudonyms in front of him. He only knows the pseudonym of his mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: They were with you at the time of -- when your valuables were taken away and at the moment of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to refer to Jasmina Vila, the late Jasmina Vila, your relative.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that your mother had more precise and reliable information, your mother VG-18, as to what had become of Jasmina Vila or what had happened to Jasmina Vila before this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree. My mother was an adult.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I respect my mother above anybody else as well. Now we're coming to one area that is crucial to me. Do you want to have your statement before you, or should I just put questions to you like this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please, if we could have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: P74. 74. Page 4. In English and also in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 3 in the Bosnian version, and paragraph 2 in English. "One of them entered the kitchen and introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you describe it for me? How was it that he introduced himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just be allowed to read this through? The question was how he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Did he come before you and say I'm Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't just him who entered the house. Three of them did. The people there knew them right away. I was at the far end of the living-room and there were many people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you give me the words with which he introduced himself? Did he say, "People, my name is Sredoje Lukic"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a few people knew right away that it was Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You said clearly here he came and introduced himself. So you said that he introduced himself. Did he use the following words: "My name is Sredoje Lukic. Good day to you people"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said that as he got into the room, and I heard other people say so later on, because this was a room full of people, and they heard him say that, and that's how this whole thing started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Witness. Are you saying that Sredoje Lukic introduced himself by saying, "My name is Sredoje Lukic. Good day to you people"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. I didn't quote his words this way. This was upstairs. There were stairs there, and there were people there who knew him by name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't -- that he said expressly those words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did Sredoje Lukic say anything in your hearing to identify himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you at some time come to the understanding that that person was Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And how did you arrive at that knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were people in the house, the older ones, who knew him, and when they left they said, "That's the policeman who works at -- in Visegrad." There were people there, including elderly women, who knew him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They said, "That's the policeman." Did they go further to identify the name of the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, your statement today is somewhat different from what you said in your written statement. You were quite explicit here and said, "One of them got into the kitchen and introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic. He carried a sniper rifle and a camouflage uniform."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: These are your words.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, these are details that cannot be described, because the -- they were not entering that house --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you scroll down in the English version, please. A little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a signature somewhere at the bottom here, your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, when testifying before this honourable Tribunal, your mother, VG-18, claimed that somebody entered the house and introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, why don't you put that question to her? She knows about this better than I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Does it sound a bit illogical to you to say -- for a person to come into the house and say, "I introduce myself, my name is Sredoje Lukic, and I will be doing this and that to you"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course it's illogical, but they were proud of that. They prided themselves on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please help me identify the individual who introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how would I be able to help you? Can you explain it to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm putting questions to you, and you're answering them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead. Fire away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, it wasn't very clear to me what you meant when you asked the witness to help you identify the individual who introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic. What exactly did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My questions and answers. My questions and answers from witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Only way. Only possible way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there daylight in the house at that moment, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were you able to see clearly the face of the person who introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How far away from -- were you at that point from your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was right by her side.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How far away from you was the person who introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, we're going to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the meantime we printed pseudonym sheet, so with your leave, I'd like to -- to use it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We left off when this robbing took place in the afternoon. You said that you are unable to make an identification. You told us that all the time VG-13 and VG-18 were with you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: VG-13 and VG-38. And, naturally, VG-18, your mother. How far was your mother from you at the -- at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was sitting next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: VG-13 and VG-18, how far were they at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were they close to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were many rooms. There was one room, another room, there was a kitchen, and they were all full.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Hasib Kurspahic, father of Huso Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where was he standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that you have very poor memory of these things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can barely remember who was standing where. It was full of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, did VG-13 perhaps confirm the identity of these men who entered the house to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty per cent of people confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about VG-13.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about VG-13. I wasn't with her. She was maybe in some corner. There were 50 or 60 people altogether there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But among those people were both VG-13 and VG-38, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I know that? I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You told me today that they were involved in the incident the whole time and that they were close to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't tell you that today. They were in the file with us. They were in front of the Red Cross. They were in the house with us. Maybe she left the room for five minutes to go to the toilet. Maybe she went out for two minutes. She wasn't with me all the time so that I could follow her movement. There were many people.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that you cannot provide us with any better information about the appearance of Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Sredoje Lukic and Milan Lukic were there and a third man whose identity I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But you cannot give me any information about how they looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty per cent of the people --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, please listen carefully to my questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty per cent of people knew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm giving you this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about your knowledge. I'm not asking you about what other people knew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, sir, I listened to people who were older than me, and they knew these men very well. I was a 14-year-old boy. I listened to what my elders were telling me, and there were some elderly people who knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was Hasib Kurspahic one of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who searched the people and took their money and their jewellery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic were in charge of collecting money and gold. The third man was searching people in another room, this third man whom I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain how come that you changed this information about the identity in your -- today's testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? What kind of change?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, please look at the statement. In this paragraph here you described Sredoje Lukic. You said that he had a sniper rifle on him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Today, transcript page 23, line 13, you said that it was Milan who had a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, these are all automatic weapons as far as I am familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that there is a significant difference between an automatic rifle and a sniper rifle, would you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is automatic weapons, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask you to listen to my questions carefully.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Visually there's a big difference, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. What is the objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Counsel hasn't established that the witness would have any basis of knowledge of these weapons, certainly at the time he was 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we look carefully at his statement, he said very explicitly that Sredoje Lukic had a sniper rifle, so he is able to distinguish between the weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did they have any hats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you at least remember who was taller and who was shorter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sredoje was older and Milan was about seven years younger as far as I could judge by their appearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. He asked about their height. Can you remember who was taller and who was shorter? He didn't ask about their age.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] VG-38 asserted that Sredoje was shorter than Milan by five centimetres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where? In which statement is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Transcript dated 2nd September 2008, lines 26, 27 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the pages slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has already given an answer to this question, so if -- if counsel's proposing to repeat the same question again about the height, the witness has already testified that he doesn't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree. He can't help you any more. Please move on, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, your mother VG-18, described Sredoje Lukic as someone who was retired at the time and that he was over 40 years of age. As for Milan Lukic, she said that he was a younger person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to ask her.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You -- do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you have to ask her. Why -- why should I give you answers on her behalf?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, no. He's not asking you to answer on behalf of your mother. What he's asking is whether you agree with your mother's description that Sredoje was someone who had retired at that time and that he was over 40 years of age.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- I can't remember that. I'm not giving any descriptions. I'll let her do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, did any of these men have any mask or a stocking over their face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. Maybe there were some other persons outside of the house. Maybe other witnesses can confirm that. As far as those inside the house were concerned, I wasn't able to notice anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember while you were moving from the Memic house to the Omeragic house who was the one who called the people to leave the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Maybe it can be found in the statements but at this moment I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In this file while you were walking in the darkness from the Memic house to the Omeragic house, the visibility was very poor, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but one could see things.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This person who introduced himself as Sredoje, do you know where he was standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the house where we were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you describe him in this particular situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. I was a little bit late. I was among the last people who entered the house. He patted me on the shoulder. Whether it was him or Milan, there were two or three of them in front of the house. Because I couldn't find my shoes, and he patted me on the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Within this particular situation would you be able to give us any description, any details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I enter the house very quickly. They were just standing in front of the house. Would that be helpful? The house where we were burned. And there were a couple of more soldiers in the dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm not denying that the incident took place and your suffering.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this is of any help.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you to help us with your answers to shed more light on who was there and who really committed this. The one that you believe was Sredoje Lukic who was standing in front of the house and who patted you on the shoulder, did he wait for the whole file to pass? So he was ahead of the column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in front of the house, and the column was moving towards him, towards the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So he was waiting for the column in front of house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: He didn't follow behind the column?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you believe the words of VG-13?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What words?
