utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honours, counsel continuously puts the words of other witnesses to this witness. Now, I submit that it's an inappropriate thing to ask this witness to judge the credibility of the other witnesses. Rather, the assertions that they made should be put to the witness. Their assertions, the factual assertions that were made can be put to the witness but not the credibility of other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We won't allow the question. Put another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to give us any detail as to the description in this situation when it was dark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What -- what darkness? There was light in front of the house. They had flashlights. Everything had been prepared in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just kindly asking you, and I'm asking you to give me answers to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So according to what you said today, you're unable to give me any better information about the person who introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic or for whom other people said that he was Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I will uphold it. Ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of any of these people who told us that it was Sredoje Lukic, or you're unable to tell us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again those were the people who knew him. I personally didn't know him. That's what I said in my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But you don't remember any specific person telling you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me see whether I understand you, Witness. You heard a number of persons saying that that was Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You knew who those persons were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But your position now is that you don't remember their names. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember their names, that's true. We were afraid of these people while we were still in our village before we moved out. We were afraid that they would come to our village, too, because they went to other villages, took men away, set houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who told you that Sredoje Lukic was working in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have heard it from someone in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned that you had heard that this group was causing incidents, did you hear about Sredoje back in April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not at that time. Not in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You testified today and you mentioned April.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't know him in April. That was the time when the Serbian army entered Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So the first information you had was on that night in Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It is missing that I said -- page 49, line 4 and 5, my question I put the name of my client, Sredoje Lukic. Information about Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, just repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this information about Sredoje Lukic that we are discussing today you heard for the first time on that day in Pionirska Street, in the village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We heard about them. We didn't see them until we left the village. The whole group, Sredoje, Milan, and another four or five men who are now walking freely around the town. There were not only these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you said that 20 per cent of the people knew that Sredoje had worked in Belgrade or that you heard that he had been working in Belgrade, how could then 20 per cent of people know Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that it was 20 per cent of the people who knew that he had worked there. Twenty per cent of the people knew him, and perhaps two of those people knew that piece of information, but the people in general knew that he was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you help us in any way in the identification, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What else do I need to tell you?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Objection. Perhaps counsel could specify exactly what question he's asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cepic, that's a very general and wide and vague question. Be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've been trying with a lot of questions in that way, but all answers are negative up till now. Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions for this witness. [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, at the time you say Sredoje Lukic and Milan Lukic entered the Mimic house, what time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around 1.00 or 2.00. It was definitely daytime.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Later as you were made to walk from the Mimic house to the Omeragic house, can you describe the visibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was good. It was good. It wasn't very good, but it was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you give some detail about why the visibility was good? Where did the light come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a light bulb outside the house, and they all had flashlight torches. Before they ordered us to move from the Memic to the Omeragic house, they had -- they took their positions outside the house. I don't know who ordered it, but they wanted to create as little noise as possible. There was a creek there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You said there was a light in front of the house. Can you say which house or which houses had lights in front of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that about the Omeragic house. I don't remember anything about that in relation to the Memic house.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall any lights on any other houses other than the Memic and the Omeragic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was some light, because there were other houses further away, and the light was coming from those other houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At the time you were in the Mimic house, when Mitar Vasiljevic addressed you and the other detainees, did he suggest to you and the others in your group that you would be safe in the Mimic house?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. It is leading. You can't lead in re-examination. Reformulate. Ask him what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: VG-84, do you recall what Mitar Vasiljevic said to you when you and the other detainees were in the Mimic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I do. He told us that we were safe there, that nobody was allowed to touch us, and that we would be spending the night there and that on the following day at 12.00 we would be heading for Orlovo and Kladanj. We would be leaving from the Red Cross building.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And did that information make you and the others feel safer in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And was that one of the reasons that you and the others remained in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had to remain in the house. We had no where else to go, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would the presence of a police officer, who the group would have known, contributed to your belief that you would be safe in that house?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Speculation, Your Honours, speculation. And what is the base for this kind of question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think the witness must be able to say whether the police officer being there would make him feel safer. Would a police officer being there, Witness, make you feel any safer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The presence of who? Which policeman?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You testified earlier that to the knowledge of the people around you, they informed you that this was Sredoje Lukic, and you learned from them that he had been a police officer. So my question is: Would the presence -- would the present of a police officer under those circumstances have made you and the others feel safer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they didn't get come there to protect us. They came there to take our valuables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Misleading question, Your Honour. Completely misleading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic says it's leading. Ms. Marcus, do you have anything further?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, sir, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to find out how long you expect to be with the witness Vasiljevic. You have already given us an estimate. Will you be more than one day, a session lasting a day?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. In fact, I think I will be substantially less with Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's clear, Your Honour, what my intention is to do with Mr. Vasiljevic is not ask to him any follow-up questions but simply to lay the foundation for admission of his prior testimony and highlight some of the relevant portions. He testified for a very, very long time about many issues and simply to highlight for the Chamber the issues that are directly relevant for the Chamber here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, any estimate of the time that you'll spend in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's sort of something that's still in development, Your Honour. Just -- and it's because of this: Obviously the Drina River is going to hinge a lot -- to a huge degree on Mr. Vasiljevic. In the trial he testified and what we have are two binders with about that much prior testimony of which we kind of have to look at and digest. I'd like to think that I could really shorten it because the points I'm trying to make will be relatively focused, but if there's a lot of testimony, that's the kind of thing, especially depending on the cooperative nature of the witness sometimes it goes easy, sometimes it goes harder. But -- so I'm having a real hard time estimating simply because the transcript of Vasiljevic is a long one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My estimation is, Your Honour, at this moment less than one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: One hour. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But I have to keep reserve at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. No. The reason for asking is that although this is primarily a matter for the Prosecution, the Chamber would like to see the evidence of that witness concluded by Thursday. So if -- if he were brought first thing on Wednesday and you were to spend less than a day's session, then I believe we should be able to conclude his evidence by the end of Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe that's entirely reasonable, Your Honour. In fact my fear is that we'll run short. So I'm trying to make arrangements to have additional witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Groome. Well, have him ready then for Wednesday, Wednesday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, I understand we're sitting in the afternoon, yes, on Wednesday. Yes, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, before this witness takes the oath and puts on the headphones may I ask the Court for -- to have one hour with this witness in my 92 ter examination? And the reason is this witness is elderly and very fragile, and it might take a little bit longer to get through what would not take as long with other witnesses. So I would ask the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may begin, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This witness has been granted protective measures --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: This witness has been granted protective measures as to facial distortion. And I would like to ask the witness if you could move closer to the microphone, please. And as I stated, Your Honour, this witness is testifying pursuant to Rule 92 ter as per the oral decision of this Court on the 1st of September, 2008, permitting the Prosecution to introduce into evidence her prior transcript and statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Witness, you don't have to read out the date. I'm just asking if the date of your birth and the name that is on the sheet, if that is your name and your date of birth. That's just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We ask that this pseudonym sheet be admitted in evidence, Your Honour. Sorry, may the witness sign this paper, then we will ask it be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P81, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave just to request admission of pseudonym sheet which we used with Witness VG-84.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. If that hasn't been admitted then we will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D10, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I would ask the court officer's assistance again in handing a pseudonym sheet for other witnesses that this witness may be referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And, Madam Witness, what is going to be handed to you at this time is a sheet of paper that has the name of some persons and their pseudonym numbers, and I'm going to ask that if you want to refer to any of these persons in your testimony that you refer to them only by the number that has been assigned to them, and please refrain from mentioning their names on the record as these witness also have protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you understand what I've asked you to do, Witness, with regard to if you mention these witnesses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I understand. It's just I'm not sure if I'll be able to read this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll just proceed and see how it goes. Witness 18, how old are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Sixty-seven.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what is your highest level of education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I completed four years of primary school in Jagodina.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And in 1992, can you tell us in which municipality you were living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you some questions, madam, about prior testimony and a prior statement that you gave to an ICTY investigator. We're going to go over a couple of changes that you wish to make to the testimony in the statement, so I'll be asking you question by question. Did you testify in the Vasiljevic trial on the 8th of October, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And since coming to The Hague this week, have you had an opportunity to review this testimony in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes. And I always have it in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, we discussed a couple of changes, and if -- with the Court's indulgence I would like to refer to the page of the transcript and lead the witness to some extent so that changes can be made. Thank you. Now, in your transcript at e-court page 28, you say that you were -- first you were in the house of Jusuf Memic. That's what it says in your testimony. Do you wish to make a change to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It seems to me that we were in Mujo's house. Therefore, his son's house, but I'm not sure. I believe that we were in Mujo's house judging by some of the photographs of the children I was able to see there, but I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us the last name of Mujo, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Memic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And do you know where Mujo Memic's house was in relation to Jusuf Memic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I do. I do, because that's where my teacher resided. She also taught my children in Prelovo. I would go to her house to discuss with her the absences from school of my children. That's how I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your testimony at page 30 in e-court, you state that --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but it would be useful for us if we have that page on our screens just to compare with our notes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I was trying to save time, but if the court could please bring up -- excuse me. It's 65 ter number 92. And it's e-court page 30. May I just -- may I see the previous page, Your Honours, please, and to scroll down? I'd like to see the page -- the actual page of the transcript, if I may. No. This is the page, sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At line 22 it begins, and if I may read it to the witness, your testimony said: "Sredoje Lukic came with the people. He introduced himself. I wouldn't have recognised him, but he introduced himself and said he was Sredoje Lukic ..." Now, could we move down a bit to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the number of page in Vasiljevic case?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That was 15 --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- 82. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, could we go back to the bottom of 1582, please, again. The bottom of this page and the top of the next page. One moment, Your Honour. We'll go back to 1582, Your Honours. We'll go back to 1582, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Where you say that Sredoje introduced himself to you, do you wish to add anything to that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, no. I mean, what else could I add? I didn't know why he came there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How did you -- okay. Strike that. Other than the -- other than the change that we just made with regard to the name of the Memic house, is everything else in your testimony true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. If we do ever come across something we can correct it, but I believe that it is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you did listen to your testimony in full, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And as you listened to the testimony, everything rang true to you when you listened to it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, no. I was mentioning Sredoje more than Milan, whereas Milan was the first one in everything. Sredoje was a bit older than him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. But, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: There's an objection, I guess?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just wrong interpretation in transcript. Page 60, line 25, witness said, "Sredoje je bio starija osoba."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Which being translated is what?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Older than Milan, and it is -- but it is completely different sense. That is my humble opinion, that she said clearly Sredoje Lukic was older person or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Isn't that what is in the transcript, that Sredoje was a bit -- down here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honours? No. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just ask the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: As you listened to your testimony, even though you may wish to add some things to your testimony, is everything in that testimony accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Everything I said is true, but perhaps those who took statements, when they printed them maybe they made some mistake, but I'm ready to correct any statement I made if necessary. I am not here to tell lies, and I am going to tell only the truth. And if I was nervous and made a mistake, I'm not nervous here. I'm going to tell you the truth because I'm talking about my people. They are also part of my people. I didn't know them, and we had two religions in Eastern --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Madam Witness, we'll get to that in a minute, but I'm just asking you if there are any changes that you wish to make, any changes meaning anything that is not correct in your prior testimony that you listened to the other day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I heard more about Sredoje than Milan. It should be the other way around. Sredoje and these dates relating to this incident were not congruent. I only remember it was the fourth day of the Bajram, and that is correct. And as for other things, I'm not quite sure that they ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Other than those changes, if you were asked the same questions today that were put to you in your former trial, would your answers be substantively the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Whatever I know and whatever is true, that's what I'm going to tell you. What I don't know I will not tell. I don't remember what I said at the time. Whatever you asked me and if that is the truth, I will repeat it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, we ask that the prior testimony be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P82, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now we ask the court usher to bring up 65 ter number 180.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Madam Witness, you remember giving a statement to a Tribunal investigator on the 4th of February, 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And again, you had a chance to review this statement, didn't you, in your language when you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And again, in your statement, which is on page 6 in both versions, the Bosnian and English, you again mention the house of Jusuf Memic. And we're going to correct that, is that correct, to say Mujo Memic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I don't know what the Court wants me. These are father and son and that was the same household, but it's up to you to decide.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm just asking if -- again, we have to make the change to your statement and put it on the record, and you just told us --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I know that this was the house of Mujo Memic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is everything contained in your statement true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And if you were asked the questions today that the investigator asked you, would your answers be substantively the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes, they would.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, we ask that statement be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P83, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, your prior testimony and your statement have both been admitted in evidence so that the Judges can read everything that you have to say about the ordeal that you experienced so I'm not going to ask you to repeat everything, but I'm going to ask you some questions. Now, in your testimony and in your statement you have mentioned two dates, the 14th of July and the 14th of June. Now, as you sit here today, do you remember if this event happened in June or July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I cannot tell you precisely. I know exactly, and I will remember that until the day I die that it was the fourth day of our great holiday Bajram and that it was a Sunday. As for the date, whether it was the 13th of this month or that month or the 14th, I really cannot tell you. Please don't bother me with that. I know that it was the fourth day of the Bajram.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now I would like to draw your attention to that date that is in your mind and to the time of approximately 5.00 in the evening. Can you tell us where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: We were in the house of Mujo Memic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When you say "we," who is "we"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: All my people. All my fellow villagers. Maybe with the exception of two households, Avdo Kurspahic and Hasan Kurspahic who had -- who had gone to visit their children in town, and the rest of my people who had been living in this village up to that point, we were all there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And had you met any of these men before this evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't. I didn't know them. I heard that he was on the police force, I mean Sredoje. I didn't have any contact with the police before. Whether he came to the village, I also don't know that. Milan I had never seen before. And as for this neighbour allegedly from Greben, I didn't know him and didn't see him before, that is to say until the time when he ordered us to take our clothes off.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, when they introduced themselves did you hear their voices clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: We heard them. There were men at the door of another room, and we heard those surnames mentioned, but we didn't see them until they came and told us to go to one room. When we entered the room I wasn't looking at Sredoje or Milan. I just remember that these two surnames were mentioned. But we were afraid to look at them, let alone to ask them who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, when you -- you refer to surnames. What do you consider to be the surname? Is it the first or the second name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Theirs you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, you mentioned in the transcript "surname." What is a surname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: For example, Milan is the first name, Lukic is the second name. Every person has two names, the first name and the last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So when you -- you say you remember two surnames were mentioned. Is that what you mean, two surnames were mentioned or two first names were mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Two first names and two last names. I said two names and two surnames, and I didn't know anything about the third man. That's why I'm not saying anything about him. I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you heard their names being mentioned by other people in the room. Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. I heard -- it was quiet when they appeared at the door. It was quiet, and I heard personally about these two. And for -- as for the third man, one person asked who this man is, and then he said that he knew his father. I'm talking about the third man. And for these two I heard it 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, during the course of the evening, did you hear their names being mentioned by anyone else in the room? Did you discuss these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, there was no point in discussing anything. We just talked about this thing. I was lying there. I didn't go out. I just heard my neighbour saying about the man from Greben, and he said, "How come he is here?" Because this village is two kilometres away. "How come he is here?" That's what we discussed, and he said that he should really be ashamed, because all of us could -- we were old enough to be his mother and he ordered us to strip naked.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: During the time period that these three men were at Memic house, did you have an opportunity to see their faces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, yes. Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And did you hear them speaking to each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you hear them speaking in general to other occupants in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Could be. They ordered us to do our job. I don't know whether they talked to other people. We thought that we were doomed. I don't know. Maybe they talked. I don't know. I wouldn't speculate about anything that I know nothing about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: My question, Madam Witness, is did you have an opportunity to hear their voices during that time they were at the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. When they arrived, they said, "Give us cash and gold. Put everything on the table." He took a knife out of his boot and said, "This is what we are going to use if we find even the slightest coin on anyone. We want all the money and the gold." This is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When you say he took a knife, can you tell us who "he" is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I would say Milan. He was in the forefront. I'm not sure. Sredoje was there, but it was Milan who did this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, how long did these men stay this time -- stay at the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Until we gave them all the money and the jewellery. I had some money on me. And my sons came to me and said, "Give them -- give it to them, mother. They're going to kill us." And I gave all the money that was intended for my children's education and for everything else. I never thought about weapons. I was just taking care of my children. They took, I don't know, all my jewellery and put it on the table. I buried my gold in the garden. I gave them the money.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness. My question -- my next question is, though, after giving them the valuables, did other things happen in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think it was Milan who said that we will go to a room in twos and threes, that they would strip us naked. I was the first next to the door, and I entered the room. This man whose name I don't know was sitting on a chair. There was a rifle next to him. Another two persons came into the room with me, and he told me to take my clothes off. I took my blazer off and a sweater. He probably wanted to search me to see whether there was any money or jewellery hidden. And then he said, "Can you see this finger of mine? This is how I want to see you." This was horrible. I took my blouse off and my underwear. It just -- well, off. That was horrendous. That was worse than being killed. I had lived with my husband for 40 years. I had three children by him. I couldn't behave like that in front of him, in front of this young man, and I was old enough to be his mother. And after that, I don't remember how things went on, how I got dressed again. I heard my boy crying. I thought that he was going to be killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I don't remember anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Madam Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've been told by my colleague who does speak Bosnian that there was a word left out on the record, so I'm going to ask the witness a question and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam Witness, when they were doing this to you or just before they did this to you, did they call you any names or did they say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: These two didn't, but the other one when we were taking our clothes off he used to call us "balija." He asked about the whereabouts of my husband. I told him that he was in Montenegro, that he went through the woods. He called me "balija." As for the other two, they didn't. Whether they entered this room or not, I don't know. Some say that Milan did. I don't know. And they were searching the men. No, no, not these two.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, can I -- how long did all of this take? Can you just give us an approximate time that these men were in this house with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I don't know. There were a lot of women there, and they all took turns. After that I went to this room and laid down. The women were ushered in twos or threes. They were also searching men. Perhaps one hour and -- or one hour and a half. I didn't have a wristwatch. How can I know the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: But during this time, was it you were in fear and were you thinking about the circumstances and who was around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Some other heard there, but I'm not going to talk about it because I didn't see it with my eyes. One could hear something from outside the house. I'm not here to speak about anything that I personally didn't see or go through.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, at some point these men left, and then did they return to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: They collected the jewellery and the money and said, "We are going now to spend it on food and drink." They got into the car in which they had arrived, and when they were at the door Jasmina was next to me. She was washing my face, and he said, "You, Vila, and you in the leather jacket come out." She was a young woman, maybe 17 or 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And who is -- who is he? You said, "He said, 'You, Vila, and you in the leather jacket, come out.'" Who said that if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Milan said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And then after this event did they leave the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: All the three of them went and these two women went with them. I was lying on the ground. Jasmina came again, crouched next to me because she was in my house at the time when we left. That was in Koritnik. And she came again to wash my face. I was so ashamed to ask her what she was told. She asked her sister-in-law, but I didn't hear what she replied. Actually, she didn't say anything. She just averted her eyes. I don't remember her -- telling her anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, after the three men -- did you notice what -- anything about the vehicle -- or did they come in a vehicle and, if so, did you notice anything about the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: They came in a car, and they went away in a car. The women didn't get into the car. I don't think so. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you hear the car leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes. It was a very noisy car, as if it didn't have an exhaust pipe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what did the occupants of this room do after the men left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Whether they came before or later, two soldiers came. The men were sitting up there, and they just said, "You and you, come out to bury two dead bodies." Then again, "You and you, come out. There are two bodies in the creek." And the four men went out with these men while two went towards Nezuci and the other two went towards Babin Potok, that is to say, to bury two corpses. They came back. They were not maltreated. They said that they had buried Safet, our vet, and his wife. And the body in Nezuci was Alija, and my neighbour said you just couldn't go near him. He was full of maggots.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. When you were in the room at this time did any of the people talk about what had happened with the men who were there at the house earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes, Edhem said, and I heard him say that, "Imagine these bastards who came among their people." I heard him saying the full name of this young man, who his parents were. I wasn't paying attention. I just remember that he mentioned his nickname, Lalco. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was there any discussion about Milan and Sredoje Lukic during this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: No, no. People were afraid. Well, they said nicely, "We are not going touch you. The following day you will be given buses to leave." If they had been treating us fairly, maybe we would have gone our ways. We wouldn't have had to go through what we did. We didn't want to disperse, because there were people who were feeble and infirm. They didn't maltreat us at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Witness. My question is, though, do you know if anyone in the room with you recognised Milan and Sredoje, and by knowing -- did anybody tell you that they knew who these men were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes. Jasmina told me that it was Milan Lukic but not -- I didn't hear anything about Sredoje. She said that it was Milan Lukic because she lived in Musici by the main road, and probably they passed by. I'm not going to go into that. Jasmina's mother can come here and she can tell you all the details. She is alive, and she's faring better than I am. I came here because my neighbours begged me to do so. I'm on medication, but I think it's better for Jasmina's mother to come here and tell you all the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, some --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is this the proper time to take the break, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, we would like to substitute the pseudonym sheet that contains the names and pseudonyms of the witnesses that may be referred to by this witness. The letters -- we had to make the letters larger so that the witness could see the names, so may we make that substitution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mrs. Witness -- sorry. Mrs. Witness, now I'd like to take you back to the Memic house and later in the evening and ask you if anyone returned to the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That probably is my fault. Later in the evening did anyone, any of the men that you saw earlier in the day, come back to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: To Memic's?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At some point did you leave the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And do you remember approximately what time that was?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, how is it that you came to leave the Memic house? Was there something that happened that caused you to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, we were sitting, the children were asleep. The same car arrived as before, the one that arrived at 5.00 p.m., just before dark. They got out of the car and outside the house, under the windows, a man approached the door and told us that we should leave, that we were not safe there, that Green Berets were arriving from up there and that we should move over to the other house to be safer, that we should not take our belongings with us, that we would be picking them up later.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, when you say the same car arrived as before, how do you know that it was the same car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, I knew the car. We heard the sound. One of our neighbours who lived by the road told us, "Now they'll kill us and burn us." That's what she said. And even those of us who were a bit further away from her overheard her say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now did you know who the soldier was who approached the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you. It must have been one of the two, but I can't be precise, because as soon as they arrived the people became upset. The children had to be woken. There were women among us who had children aged 1 or 3, and there was a lot of noise all of a sudden. People were protesting about having to move to the other house. They said, "Why should we move to that other house?" I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly. One of the two did arrive. I knew by the sound of their voice that it was the same ones who had been there before.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And who were the -- who were those -- who were they? You have to put that on the record and tell the Judges what you mean by "they." Who were the same ones who had been there before? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, who else but Sredoje and Milan. One of the two approached the door only, but they were the only ones who knew that we were there. They were the ones who left us there. By their voice, by the sound of the car, and by the story that he told us politely, we knew who he was. He wasn't one of us, but he was quite polite, and he told us that we had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And did any of the other persons in the house other than the woman you just mentioned saying "They'll kill us and burn us," did anyone say the names of those people? Did anyone talk about who these men were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Everybody was shouting, "The Lukics. Here. The Lukics are coming again." There is one lady who said, "Here, the Lukics are coming over again. We're done for." *Q. So then what happened next? Did you leave the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes, we did. I was among the last to leave. (redacted) (redacted) so I was among the last to go down to that house. They were on both sides in relation to us as we were moving to the other house, and as we reached the door of the house there were perhaps three or four of them milling around us. People were getting into the house, and as soon as I heard those other women say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. It's been brought to my attention that there's a reference that should be redacted, or should we be in closed session? Are you going to -- are you going to be on this subject?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, I think we should probably go into closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think page 75, line 17, name, just to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we saw that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, it's line 15, but I think she's going to be talking about what happened, and she may be referring to this person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And when -- and you say you left -- you left the Memic house. You went to another house. Do you remember whose house that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I do. It was the house of Adem Omeragic, whose sister with her daughter-in-law and two children came there to spend the night in that house since we were supposed to take the bus the following morning, the following day. I do remember that this was the house belonging to this neighbour's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And how long did it take you to walk from the Memic house to this second house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Less than 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And did you see any of the men that were escorting the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes, we did, but we didn't dare to look directly at them. We looked at their feet and made sure that we went to where we were told to go. We didn't dare to watch them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did they speak with you at all as you were walking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: No, not at all. They were making fun. And as I was the last one to enter, he told me, "Get in, balija. What are you waiting for? Where is Alija now to help you?"

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So this is -- when you say you were the last one to enter, are you talking about entering the Omeragic house now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, precisely. I mean the Omeragic house. I was the last one to enter the house or the last but one. Perhaps there was another woman behind me. I know that there was no space in the room. It was so full of people that I hesitated at the door, and he pushed me inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You say "he," "he pushed me inside," and "he told me --"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: A soldier. A soldier. I don't know who he was. I didn't look him in the face.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you recognise his voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: But he was one of those who -- yes. It was those people who told us to move. He was with us as we set out from the other house.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And, Madam Witness, you have to tell us who "those" are. You have to tell the Judges who "those" are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, the Lukics, who else? I've said this so many times now. Now, whether it was Milan or Sredoje, I didn't lift my head to see which one was next to me. I didn't dare to. I was trying to make sure that I know where I was heading rather than looking at who was it who was pushing me ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: But you heard the voice of the person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Even now I remember that there was something pushing me in the back. I don't know whether it was a rifle or something else, but I do recall those words, "Where is Alija now to help you?"

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And was the person -- the voice that you heard say, "Where is Alija now to help you," is that the voice of someone that you had seen earlier in the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Leading and unduly suggestive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Next question, Ms. Sartorio. It was leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The person who said, "Where is Alija now to help you," did you recognise that voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, yes. It must have been one of the two who told us that, one of those who came to the house, because he accompanied us all the way. There were others on the other side, but this one was following us to make sure that we all got there, and I was among the last ones, so he was following me, and he was the one who said, "Where's Alija now to help you?"

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And when you heard this, did you associate this voice with any person --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me hear the rest of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That was the question. Did you associate this voice with any person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would say asked and answered at that point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think that's leading. Answer the question. Did you associate that voice with any person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. It was either Sredoje or Milan. Who else could it have been? Yes. That was what they wanted to do, to finish us off. I realised as I was coming to the house that this is where we all meet our end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But can you say which of the two the voice belonged to? You said it was either Milan or Sredoje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say that. I didn't look them in the face to see which one was saying those words. One of them was following me, and most probably it was the one who came to the house and that must have been Milan. But I didn't look him in the face. When they were talking, I didn't dare to look up. I just proceeded on my way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So now, Witness, please tell the Chamber after you got into the second house, tell them what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: When I entered the house they closed the door. A burst of fire was shot. The door was opened again and they said, "Listen, can you hear the Green Berets shooting up there beyond Babin Potok?" They closed the door again. The people inside were crying. They were upset. We knew that they were either going to kill us all or burn us. I turned toward the window, and as I reached the window I lost control. There was my child there. I reached the window, and as the door opened, a flame appeared as large as the door itself. I turned toward the window trying to smash the pane to let some air in. There was smoke that was choking me. I placed my left hand on my mouth, and I used my right hand to smash at the window. I tried five or six times before the windowpane was smashed. I tried to go out that way, and I heard a grenade explode. There was a sort of a mesh there that was on my way, and I had trouble going through the window, but my child approached me from the back and pushed me out of the window. I felt something wet on my hand. It was a bit paralysed. My child pushed me out of the window and said, "Let's run away, mom." I was unable to run, so he pulled me towards the creek, and as he pulled me by the creek we got into it. At that point there was light from a flashlight torch behind us, but we managed to duck down, cross the creek and hide behind the tree. They turned toward other individuals who were trying to run for their lives. It had been raining the whole day and night. We spent the night by the creek and then went up where we found a safe place to hide. We listened for -- we listened to the screams and moans for an hour or two. We were by the creek, crouching one by the other. We heard somebody coming up the creek. We were afraid that they were looking for us, but it was one individual who managed to get away and who went past us. We didn't dare shout to the person for fear that we would be discovered. The person went up the creek, and it was another individual who managed to survive and flee the fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Could you tell us if you know that person and any other persons who escaped the fire that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Yes, I know the person. Had they all managed to escape, I would not be the only one to go back to my village, the only one alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you give us the names of the persons that you know survived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Let me see here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You're in closed session, so you can use the names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Under number 13, and number 38, and number 84.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And do you know many of the persons who perished in that fire that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Of course. Of course I do. I had been living with them for 28 years. Of course I knew them. I was there when they were born, when they were married. I know them all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Witness 18, can you tell the Chamber what impact this ordeal has had on your life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I cannot find the words to describe that. I'm already nearing my end, but number 84 ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Shall we proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Witness, would you like to tell the Chamber what impact this ordeal has had on your life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: It had impact in every possible way. I've become forgetful. My nerves are at the end of their tethers. I'm restless. I suffer from high blood pressure. Whenever I go to Visegrad or to that village of mine, there are ladies calling me for a cup of coffee here and there. I go over there, cry my heart out and then come back home. That's how I feel. That's -- it's no way to feel that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'd like to ask you, if you would, if you would take a look around this courtroom and carefully look at everyone and tell me if you recognise anyone in this courtroom other than myself and Mr. Groome and Amir Zec. Could you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: Well, of course I do recognise. They are my people too. I didn't come here to say things that are not true or to lie. I'm almost 70. Of course I can recognise them. They went to school with my children. Milan might even be of the same age as my children. But I have to. I have sworn that I would come here and speak the truth for all those whose children perished, parents perished. Let me swear and let me swear by number 84 that I didn't utter a single word that would not be inaccurate, and I swear by this number 84 with whom I have been living alone since the end the war. Of course I know them. I know them both. I'm very sorry, but I have to speak up because my village has remained deserted and empty. There's nobody there. You can hear the birds chirping in the forest but I have no one there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I would just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I would like to find out the significance of 84.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, then we may have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Madam, you did answer -- you talked a minute ago about knowing some persons. You have to say on the record the names of these persons and -- and describe them. This has to be on the record, if you would. So please tell us who you recognise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Alarid is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we again would object to the unduly suggestive nature of this identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She has been asked to -- she has been asked to say on record the names of the persons, and we hear the objection you have made. The witness is to provide the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot be more precise. It's been so many years. Which is which? Which is Milan, which is Sredoje, I can't do this. I only know that one of them is Milan and the other one is Sredoje, but I can't be more precise than that. I can't. My eyesight is very poor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. One last question. May we bring up the transcript that was admitted in evidence and -- that's Exhibit number 82, Your Honours, and page 52 in e-court, please. It's page 1604 of the transcript. Could you scroll down. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At the bottom, you were asked about a person being called Mico or Milorad. We can go to the top of the next page, please. Now, when you were asked about Mico or Milorad, do you know who this person is that you were being asked about? Who is Mico or Milorad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I know Mico from Lipovac [as interpreted]. His name is Milorad or something like that -- or, rather, Milorad Lipovac is his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18
utterances.text: I know him from Podgreben.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered the condition of the witness, who is obviously distressed, and we believe that we should adjourn at this time and allow her to recompose herself over the weekend. So we will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, but I had notified the legal officer earlier there is an important matter that I did want to bring to the attention of the Chamber. If that would be possible to do that perhaps after excusing the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we do this in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.
